query: Single-phase high-entropy alloys have difficulty achieving a satisfactory strength–ductility balance. Earlier work introduced the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy with a uniform, fine lamellar structure to enable large-sized production and obtain good strength and plasticity, but its performance still falls short of industrial requirements. Its use in aircraft and spacecraft fasteners further requires stability under extreme temperature fluctuations, long-term mechanical loading, room-temperature creep, and corrosion, while relevant creep and corrosion studies remain limited by sample-size and experimental-environment constraints. Given these limitations and design requirements, what single intervention could improve the alloy’s practical performance? Present one hypothesis that specifies the intervention, causal mechanism, predicted improvement over the starting material, boundary conditions, supporting prior evidence, and a feasible experiment whose outcome could falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a small, controlled addition of tungsten (W) into the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy will enhance its resistance to room-temperature creep and corrosion while maintaining or improving its strength–ductility balance.
generation.material_initial_state: AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy with a uniform, fine lamellar structure that currently underperforms industrial requirements under extreme temperature fluctuations and long-term mechanical loading.
generation.intervention: Doping the alloy with a minor amount (e.g., 1–3 at.%) of tungsten during alloy preparation.
generation.conditions: The alloy will be subjected to industrial service conditions including extreme temperature fluctuations (e.g., from -50°C to 300°C), sustained mechanical loading (to simulate long-term use and room-temperature creep), and corrosive environments relevant to fastener applications in aerospace.
generation.structural_mediator: The tungsten is expected to refine and stabilize the lamellar microstructure by promoting solution strengthening and possibly forming thermally stable nano-precipitates that hinder dislocation motion.
generation.mechanism: Tungsten atoms, being refractory, are anticipated to enhance load transfer within the alloy and act as pinning centers for dislocations, thereby reducing creep rates. In addition, the stabilized microstructure may exhibit improved passivation, leading to better corrosion resistance under aggressive conditions.
generation.predicted_outcome: W-doped alloy samples will show lower creep rates, improved corrosion metrics (e.g., reduced corrosion current density), and an equal or improved balance of tensile strength and ductility compared to the undoped baseline alloy.
generation.baseline: Performance metrics of the current AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy including its creep rate, corrosion performance, tensile strength, and ductility under the same testing conditions.
generation.boundary: This intervention is anticipated to be effective within the temperature range of approximately -50°C to 300°C and under loading conditions typical for aerospace fasteners. Outside these conditions or with substantially higher dopant levels, the beneficial effects may not be observed.
generation.uncertainty: There is uncertainty regarding the exact influence of tungsten on phase stability and the potential formation of deleterious phases; experimental data on tungsten additions in this eutectic system are limited.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of alloy samples: one batch with the standard composition and one with 1–3 at.% tungsten doping. Subject both batches to standardized tests including constant-load creep tests at room temperature, cyclic thermal shock tests from -50°C to 300°C, and electrochemical corrosion tests in a simulated corrosive medium. Carry out microstructural analysis before and after testing.
measurements: Quantitative creep rate (strain rate under constant load)
Electrochemical metrics (corrosion potential and current density)
Tensile testing for strength and ductility measurement
Microstructural characterization (SEM/TEM analysis for lamellar stability and precipitate formation)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the tungsten-doped samples do not exhibit a statistically significant reduction in creep rate, improvement in corrosion resistance, or maintenance/improvement of the mechanical strength–ductility balance compared to the undoped alloy, the hypothesis will be falsified.
